files.label: Reine — étude de machine de ponte
files.review: Étude du grand arc nervuré, des brides et de la masse organique lobée, sans la caméra de tournage visible dans une référence. L’anatomie et les petits mécanismes sont reconstruits à partir de deux photos de 333×167. Les chaînes sont tronquées en haut du cadre : 64 pixels alpha≥128 touchent le bord. Candidat documentaire incomplet ; aucune admission runtime, aucun plafond ou ancrage fictif ajouté à la salle.

Mécanismes et anatomie fine reconstruits

Ne remplace ni la Reine ni son palan dans la campagne

prompts.snowcatPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: one transparent lateral 2D vehicle sprite for the landing area of the AVP (2004) DLC.
Input 1: the previous generated Snowcat. Edit target for 2D rendering style and left-facing orientation only. Its all-grey cab, excessively elongated proportions, cargo bags and tall rear box must not be treated as references.
Input 2: actual film frame in the Piper Maru hold. This is the main authority for cabin colour, cab shape, metallic rear loading platform, lights and industrial details. The cabin is RED, not grey or white.
Input 3: actual film frame of the Snowcats at night outdoors, auxiliary reference for tracks, layout and field use.
Primary request: make one corrected Weyland expedition PistenBully Snowcat matching these film references as closely as they allow. A compact angular red enclosed cab with broad dark windows, black continuous tracks under the vehicle, simple metallic grey rear loading deck, restrained steel handrails, and amber warning lamps. The front faces LEFT. Include the simple front snow-plow blade documented for the production miniature, connected by a believable short lifting linkage. The rear must remain an open industrial loading platform, not a tall enclosed truck body or a pile of invented luggage.
Keep the cabin-to-deck proportions close to the film. Do not add a turret, weapon, personnel, duplicate vehicle, oversized wheels or fantasy machinery. Do not invent registration numbers or illegible lettering: leave small ambiguous markings unobtrusive rather than assigning one vehicle's number to the whole fleet.
Composition: entire vehicle in clean readable side elevation, approximately eye-level camera, modest shallow depth only if needed for legibility. All blade, tracks, lamps and antenna within the frame, minimum 6 percent transparent margin. Wheels/track contact line horizontal.
Style: detailed hand-painted 2D game asset, cold restrained lighting, red paint clearly visible with slight weathering, realistic steel and rubber. No dramatic bloom, no detached pieces, no snowfield, no cast ground shadow, no sky, no opaque background, no text label or watermark.
Exactly ONE independent vehicle sprite on true transparent background.
prompts.whalebonePrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: single transparent 2D scenery prop for the whaling station in AVP (2004).
Image 1 is the previous generated whalebone candidate, provided only as an edit target and surface-detail reference. Its museum-like complete rib cage, top vertebral column and regular arched tunnel are incorrect for this film scene.
Image 2 is the actual film frame of the protagonists at the whaling station. Use the exposed ribs in the left foreground as the authoritative shape and placement reference.
Rebuild image 1 as ONE isolated group of the exposed whale ribs seen in image 2: tall separate weathered pale bone curves, uneven spacing and heights, larger ribs to the left and progressively shorter ribs to the right, curving inward. Their lower ends disappear into the same ground-contact level. Preserve a shallow two-row depth from the film reference so the gaps remain visible. Do not connect the ribs with a top spine, a skull, a complete animal skeleton or a perfectly regular architectural arch.
Composition: readable lateral 2D scenery sprite, entire rib group within the canvas with generous empty margins. Do not copy the people, industrial tank, platforms, snowfield, sky or film-frame black bars. No base slab, cast ground shadow, labels, background glow, border or watermark.
Material: worn ivory-grey bone with restrained frost and small irregularities matching the frame, detailed painted Tantalus game style. Neutral cool diffuse lighting suitable for the existing nighttime scene. Do not add gore.
One independent asset only. Background truly transparent, including every opening between ribs. Preserve a clean ground-contact line at the rib ends without a large snow mound.
prompts.satellitePrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: one independent transparent PNG orbital satellite sprite for the AVP (2004) game bible.
Input image 1: previous generated satellite candidate. Edit target and painting-material style only; its generic two-wing geometry is wrong.
Input image 2: John Lee's actual Weyland satellite production maquette photograph. This is the authoritative reference for overall silhouette, arrangement, proportions and viewpoint, although fine detail is limited by its small resolution.
Primary request: rebuild the satellite in image 1 to closely follow image 2. Use the long narrow pale white/grey and gold cylindrical axial body, long thin axial antenna, separate small forward hub, and the several blue solar panel assemblies distributed radially on white structural arms. Reproduce the visible arrangement in the reference; do not keep the two large symmetrical rectangular wings, cube-shaped central camera bus, dish or mast from image 1.
Composition: one complete isolated satellite, same approximate oblique side view as the maquette, with every panel and antenna inside the canvas and at least 7 percent empty transparent margin around the entire silhouette. No pedestal, stand, room, planet, extra object, labels, border or watermark.
Style: detailed hand-painted 2D game asset with believable metal and solar-cell materials, restrained cool lighting and fine clean edge definition. Keep the reference topology more important than invented detail. Small unseen details must remain simple and unobtrusive. No terrestrial grime or snow.
Output: one satellite only, genuinely transparent background. This is a reference-informed candidate, not a certified exact reconstruction.
prompts.celticPrompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: one independent full-body 2D character sprite for the AVP (2004) production bible.
Input: the photograph of the screen-matched Celtic Predator production costume. It is the identity, costume, material and damage reference. Preserve Celtic's specific helmet and armour; this is not Scar, Chopper or a generic Predator.
Primary request: translate this photographed costume into a detailed hand-painted lateral game-facing idle stance, facing RIGHT, with a slight torso turn only to keep the distinctive mask and chest damage readable. Whole body, both feet, entire helmet and dreadlocks inside the canvas with clear margins. Weight balanced, arms naturally lowered, hands empty.
Preserve the broad metallic Celtic mask with its strong ridged lower face and angular crown, long dark separate dreadlocks, ochre mottled skin under black mesh, asymmetric damaged chest armour, heavy shoulder plates, brown diagonal strap and leather belt/pouches, long central loincloth, broad wrist guards, layered metal greaves and clawed armoured feet. Keep the damage visible on this reference rather than silently restoring an intact variant.
Do not copy the mannequin's display base or white photography background. Omit the display-mounted shoulder cannon because its availability in the targeted scene is not established; do not invent other weapons or props. No bare human face, no extra arms, no action scene, no gore, no blood effects, no text, no watermark.
Style: crisp high-detail 2D game painting suitable for Aliens Tantalus, restrained neutral cool illumination, believable worn metal and skin, consistent proportions from the reference. The result is a specific damaged-costume candidate for review, not a certified exact or animated character.
One character only on truly transparent background; no cast ground shadow or background glow.
prompts.queenMachinePrompt:
Use case: style-transfer
Asset type: one isolated detailed 2D production-study image for the AVP (2004) game bible.

The two attached low-resolution photographs are model-maker John Lee's practical Queen suspension/egg-laying machinery for AVP (2004). Image 1 is the main shape and attachment reference; image 2 clarifies the suspended circular assembly. Their low resolution does not establish unseen engineering or fine surface detail.

Recreate ONE coherent suspended Queen-and-ovipositor machine assembly in a readable shallow three-quarter SIDE view, with the Queen's recognisable ridged head at the LEFT, the pale ochre lobed organic egg sac extending to the right beneath a dark metallic circular/ribbed support framework. Retain the visible heavy ring structure, closely repeated radial slots and ribbed bands, metal clasps and restraint links actually connected around the organic mass. Keep the machine continuous and weight-bearing: supports touch what they support. The large organic lobes hang BELOW the upper circular structure, with the dark biomechanical Queen head and short visible upper torso emerging from the left end. Include only visible Queen anatomy needed to read the photographed suspended assembly; do not add an unrelated standing full-body Queen beside it.

The primary silhouette must be driven by the supplied photographs: a broad low horizontal grouping of rounded lobes and the heavy circular arc above/behind them. NOT a rectangular prison cage, not a rectangular computer rack, not an upright human-sized throne, not a generic spaceship engine. Maintain the photographed warm cream/ochre membranes and near-black metal/alien exoskeleton, with restrained cool neutral highlights; no blood or gore.

Style: finely painted realistic 2D game-production art, strong material separation and clear silhouette, no exaggerated glowing tech. Show the entire coherent assembly in the frame with generous transparent breathing room. Background completely transparent, including spaces through the mechanism. No set wall, no floor, no pedestal, no stars, no production camera or filming equipment (the black object at right of image 2 is not part of the fictional prop), no humans, no extra monsters, no text, logos, arrows or labels. This is a visual candidate based on low-resolution production references, not a dimensional reconstruction or a 1:1 certification.
